# Results — Study 323 (BTC-Halving) on the real BTC-USD tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The folk thesis: Bitcoin
moves in a clean four-year cycle locked to the mining **halving** — bottoming a little
before each halving, topping ~12-18 months after, then crashing into the next bottom.
We hardcode the four halving dates (2012-11-28, 2016-07-09, 2020-05-11, 2024-04-20) and
test the cycle on Yahoo `BTC-USD` daily closes. As-of **2026-06-14**; match the
fingerprint to confirm you hold the same tape.*

## Data stamp

| Series | Window | Days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| BTC-USD (Yahoo, daily, auto-adjust) | 2014-09-17 → 2026-06-14 | 4,289 | `3c26b7c8e544` |

**The binding constraint, named up front.** Yahoo's `BTC-USD` history *starts
2014-09-17*. Of the four halvings, **2012 and 2016 are not covered** by clean daily data
(2016 only from two months prior; 2012 not at all). A "four-cycle study" is in practice a
**three-window** study — and only **2020 and 2024** are post-2016-with-full-context. No
HAC machinery rescues an *n* of two-to-three cycles.

## Did the halving print the top and the bottom? — realised cycle extrema

For each halving we take the window `[halving, halving + 1458d)` and locate the price high
and low, reporting the offset in **days after the halving**. The lore predicts the high
clusters near +365..+550 days and the low near the cycle edges (just before / just after).

| Halving | window (d) | high offset (d) | low offset (d) | high (×base) | low (×base) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2012-11-28 | 1457 | **1296** | 777 | 1.68× | 0.39× |
| 2016-07-09 | 1457 | **525** | 24 | 29.95× | 0.84× |
| 2020-05-11 | 1457 | **1402** | 0 | 8.50× | 1.00× |
| 2024-04-20 | 785 (partial) | 534 | 139 | 1.92× | 0.83× |

The high offsets are **1296, 525, 1402, 534** days; the low offsets **777, 24, 0, 139**.
There is **no cluster**: each cycle prints its extrema at a wildly different phase. The
tidy "top one year after, bottom just before" is a line drawn through whichever points
already happened. **The halving does not reliably mark the top or the bottom.**

## Forward returns by cycle phase (quarters of the 4-year cycle)

Mean daily log-return within each quarter of the halving cycle (bucket 0 = the quarter
just after a halving), with a naive daily Newey-West HAC *t*:

| Bucket | phase | n days | mean (bps/day) | HAC *t* |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 | 0.00–0.25 (post-halving) | 1095 | **+31.9** | **+3.45** |
| 1 | 0.25–0.50 | 1162 | +0.3 | +0.03 |
| 2 | 0.50–0.75 | 1152 | +1.9 | +0.18 |
| 3 | 0.75–1.00 (pre-halving) | 879 | +13.7 | +1.23 |

The post-halving quarter *does* carry the strongest average return, and the daily HAC *t*
of **+3.45** looks like it clears the bar. **It does not** — that 1095-day window is fed by
only **three** halving realisations, and the per-cycle post-halving-quarter means are:

| Cycle | post-halving q0 days | mean (bps/day) |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2016-07 | 364 | +36.5 |
| 2020-05 | 364 | +52.1 |
| 2024-04 | 364 | **+7.7** |

Three points, and the most recent one is **near zero** — the effect is decaying as the
asset matures and the trade gets crowded. A daily HAC *t* treats ~1000 autocorrelated days
from three cycles as if they were independent; the honest effective *n* is **three**, and
no *t* is meaningful on three clustered realisations. **Suggestive, literature-supported,
uncertifiable on this tape → WEAK, not REAL.**

## Could you trade it? — halving-timing rule vs buy-and-hold

Long BTC during the first half of each cycle (phase `[0.0, 0.5)`, the lore's "bull"
window), else flat; one-bar fill lag, **10 bps one-way × NAV** on each flip:

| | strategy | buy-and-hold |
|---|--:|--:|
| CAGR | **+35.1%/yr** | **+52.3%/yr** |
| Sharpe (ann.) | 0.60 | 0.63 |
| time in market | 52.6% | 100% |
| flips | 8 | — |

Excess (strategy − buy-and-hold) mean = **−3.3 bps/day**, HAC *t* = **−0.92**, 95% block-
bootstrap CI **[−10.6, +4.2] bps/day**. The timing rule **underperforms simply holding
BTC**, sitting in cash through half the cycle and earning two-thirds of buy-and-hold. The
"cycle" you bought with the calendar was beta you could have had for free — minus the days
you sat out. **Tradability → MIRAGE.**

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is a faithful cycle detector

On a deterministic synthetic BTC-like tape, the same phase-bucket engine recovers the
post-halving signal **only when a halving-locked cycle is planted**:

| Planted cycle amplitude | bucket-0 mean (bps/day) | bucket-0 HAC *t* | detected? |
|---|--:|--:|:--:|
| 0.0 (pure GBM, null) | +13.3 | +1.09 | no (|t| < 2) |
| 1.5 (clean halving cycle) | +66.6 | +4.65 | yes |

The harness banks a planted cycle and finds nothing in the null — so the real-tape
bucket-0 number is a statement about *three BTC cycles*, not a machinery artefact, and the
synthetic Sharpe never backs the Signal stamp.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The post-halving quarter carries the strongest return (+31.9 bps/day,
  naive HAC *t* +3.45), but that rests on **three** halving realisations (+36.5, +52.1,
  **+7.7** bps/day — decaying), and the cycle *extrema* don't cluster at all. The lore is
  literature-flavoured and suggestive; this tape cannot certify it as REAL.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** A halving-timing rule earns +35%/yr vs buy-and-hold's +52%/yr
  (excess HAC *t* = −0.92): it underperforms doing nothing. The "cycle edge" was beta minus
  the cash drag.
- **Does the halving print the top & bottom? — BUSTED.** High offsets 1296/525/1402/534 d,
  low offsets 777/24/0/139 d — scattered across the whole cycle. The halving marks neither
  extreme reliably; the clean cycle chart is hindsight drawn through four points.
